children: lost nearly 8% in premarket trading on Thursday after failure in a mid-stage trial for remlifanserin, its experimental therapy for hallucinations and delusions associated with Alzheimer’s disease psychosis.

Referring to topline data from the Phase 2 portion of its ongoing RADIANT clinical trial, the company said that remlifanserin at 60 mg "narrowly missed" the primary endpoint of a clinical tool designed to measure the severity of the disease.

RADIANT evaluated the once-daily therapy at 60 mg and 30 mg versus placebo in patients suffering from hallucinations and delusions associated with ADP, a condition affecting roughly 30% of those with Alzheimer’s.

However, the company plans to continue enrollments in two Phase 3 studies for remlifanserin in ADP with an amendment to remove the 30 mg dose, which it said showed “minimal improvement across endpoints compared to placebo” in Phase 2 RADIANT.

As for tolerability, remlifanserin was found to have a favorable safety profile, with both doses showing adverse events, serious adverse events, and trial discontinuations due to adverse events at a similar rate

title: Acadia falls after mid-stage trial setback for Alzheimer’s psychosis therapy
